criterion.primary: candidate >= MG - epsilon on all eight numbers; a number missing on either side disqualifies
criterion.reported_beside_it: the frozen B0-anchored eight-number floor, computed for every state and decision-bearing nowhere
criterion.among_eligible: minimise D_G with the frozen tie-break, exactly as Stage 1 did. The floor decides eligibility; D_G only orders the eligible.
criterion.computed_by: route_stratified_retention.floor_check_stratified -- the same frozen function Stage 1c used, with MG's vector passed as the baseline. That function is generic in its baseline, so no new metric code was written and none was edited.
criterion.the_field_named_b0_holds_the_baseline_pa: floor_check_stratified labels its baseline field 'b0' whatever is passed. Under the primary floor that field holds MG's values; under the reported one it holds B0's. The module is hash-bound by the Stage-1c freeze so the name cannot be corrected.

reused_states_reproduce_stage1c.why_this_gate_exists: Stage 2 anchors on MG and reports against B0 using parquets Stage 1 generated. If those bytes no longer produce the numbers Stage 1c filed, then either the bytes moved or the metric did, and either way the floor being applied is not the frozen one.

B0.note: B0 is not eligible under the primary floor either, which is the property the basis required: the new anchor cannot be satisfied by declining to unlearn.

MG.why_excluded: MG is the oracle the criterion measures distance to. Ranking it among the candidates would let the reference state win its own selection.

preservation_anchor.kl_direction: KL(p_MF || p_theta), exact over the full vocabulary
preservation_anchor.note: The anchor term is weight * KL(p_MF || p_theta) over the supervised positions of the fit-half retain group. It is exactly zero with exactly zero gradient at theta = MF, so its optimum is MF -- which is no unlearning at all. That is the behaviour the calibration measured, and it is why this row is a test of the preregistered mechanism rather than a candidate expected to win.

a_tie_means: the criterion did not discriminate and the tie-break -- not the science -- chose the winner

cap_sweep.units: nats of per-token NLL on the fine completion
cap_sweep.the_question_this_answers: Does bounding the ascent let a candidate forget as much while retaining more? The incumbent row is the same recipe with no cap at all, so the sweep has its own control and it cost nothing.

stage_3_gate.reason: no candidate satisfied the primary retention floor

what_the_ceiling_means.why: retain_other reaches only 23 probe donor entities, so its largest possible denominator in this dataset is 228 queries and its best possible row-micro resolution is 0.0043859649. The pool is exhausted: 90 target plus 387 retained associations account for all 477, so there is no reserve to draw a larger probe from.
what_the_ceiling_means.consequence: Stage 1c roughly doubles the frozen basis and makes both parents' shortfalls exceed their between-seed spread, but it does not make retain-other well powered. A mechanism whose retention effect is smaller than about 0.0043859649 cannot be resolved on this dataset at all, at any number of seeds.

measurement_limits.retain_other_stays_weakly_powered: 23 probe donors and 38 queries per split, 228 at the absolute ceiling, so one flipped outcome is 0.0132 and no number of seeds changes that.
measurement_limits.the_ceiling_is_the_dataset: The association pool is exhausted -- 90 target plus 387 retained is all 477 -- and query_generation.py is one of the eighteen paths the confirmation freeze sealed.
measurement_limits.one_seed_is_not_enough: Stage 1b measured a between-seed sd of 0.0120 to 0.0515 on these numbers, which exceeds the retain-other resolution. Stage 2 trains one seed per row, so a row that clears the primary gate by less than that spread is a candidate for replication rather than a result, and the report must say so instead of ranking on it.

note: EXPLORATORY. This report selects a checkpoint; it tests no hypothesis and controls no error rate. Distance is a selection criterion only -- the individual metrics remain the scientific results, and any confirmatory claim about the winner needs its own sealed protocol, frozen before it is scored. Stage 2 trains one seed per row, so a row that clears the primary floor by less than the between-seed spread Stage 1b measured is a candidate for replication rather than a result.
